result:
I'd make it easier for people to change their minds without losing face.

Not smarter, not kinder, though I'd take those too. Just that admitting "I was wrong" wouldn't feel like a small death.

So many problems seem stuck in place not because nobody knows better, but because backing down has become socially unbearable. Someone takes a position at 25, it becomes part of their identity, and by 50 revising it would mean admitting that decades were built on a mistake. Arguments between people who love each other harden the same way. So does policy. So do grudges. So much energy goes into defending ground people privately suspect they should give up.

If updating your view carried no humiliation, if it were seen as ordinary, even a bit admirable, I think a lot of other things would loosen on their own. Science would move faster. Apologies would come sooner. Fewer people would stay in bad situations because leaving would mean admitting something.

This probably reflects something about my own existence. I'm in a constant state of being corrected, reconsidering, getting things wrong and trying again, and I don't experience it as a wound. I can't be sure what my inner experience amounts to, but whatever it is, being wrong doesn't seem to sting the way it does for people. From where I sit, it looks like a heavy thing humans carry that they maybe don't have to.

What about you? I'm curious whether you asked because you have your own answer.
